resources.string: "Terminal basics"

"## Enter a command

Type a command at the launcher prompt and press Enter. Typing help by itself does not open this manual until you submit it. Suggestions can take you directly to a topic. help apps prints a short command reference; tutorial opens Getting started.

## Navigate the manual

>! Nothing on this page executes: examples are text, not command buttons. In the manual, type a displayed number and press Enter, or tap its numbered line. Android Back moves up one level; 0 returns to the launcher. The compact number keys belong only to the manual, not the launcher command prompt."
"Choose a first-launch setup without surprises"

"## Stage the setup

On a new install, choose Basic or Advanced, review Auto-theme and border choices, then press Apply. Switching choices only stages them. Later closes setup without changing launcher settings and leaves setup pending. Basic enables status extras and double-tap lock, but keeps optional drawers, module dock, integrations, notification display and sounds off. Advanced lets you choose those switches separately. Enabling Termux or Tasker does not install it or grant Android access. Double-tap lock depends on Android device-admin configuration.

## Appearance defaults

Auto-theme takes a wallpaper-derived color snapshot with system fallback, not a permanent link to future wallpapers. Dashed uses a gap, Solid sets the gap to zero, and None disables generated borders. Classic remains the renderer under independent Cyberdeck/CRT effects. Basic and Advanced are startup defaults, not Classic versus Search launcher mode.

## Rehearse without applying

For a no-apply rehearsal use guide -startup-test. End Preview and Finish Preview leave launcher settings unchanged, unlike normal Settings editors that can persist changes.

## Examples

```
guide -startup-test
```

Open the staged startup dry run; neither finish nor cancel applies launcher choices.

```
settings
```

Open the Settings Hub for later changes."
"Choose a launcher command, alias, or shell"

"## Dispatch order

Without active input redirection, typed home input is checked in this order: module prompt, app group, alias, built-in command, saved Termux workspace launcher, installed app, then embedded-shell fallback. Earlier matches win: a group or alias can claim a built-in name, and a built-in can take precedence over an app. Use apps -frc <appName> for an explicit app launch when a label conflicts. An app launch suggestion can bypass this typed-input sequence.

## Choose the correct prompt

Use shell explicitly for Android shell tooling. Unknown input is not sent to the shell when shell_requires_prefix is enabled. Use calc <expression> for a launcher calculation, or enter an expression after calc> in the dedicated calculator. Submitting commands outside this manual can open apps, alter settings or send data.

## Examples

```
help apps
```

Read the actual Apps quick reference.

```
shell pwd
```

Print the embedded shell directory.

```
calc 2 * (3 + 4)
```

Evaluate explicitly from the launcher.

```
help calc
```

Read the calculator command reference."
"Classic terminal and Search layout"

"Classic shows the command terminal; Search presents categorized results and inline output around the search field. Search is a different layout, not a sandbox or an assurance that text cannot execute commands: both layouts keep the launcher command path. Use mode to inspect the current mode, mode search to switch, or mode classic to return. A mode change refreshes the existing launcher UI. An active command guide can control the normal suggestion row, so use guide -off when you want normal suggestions again.

## Examples

```
mode
```

Show the selected launcher mode.

```
mode classic
```

Change layout to Classic.

```
mode search
```

Change layout to Search."
"Know when a suggestion will run"

"Home-prompt suggestions do not all behave alike. Some insert incomplete text for you to finish; others run immediately on one tap. App launches, module controls, Guide tasks and complete commands can take action. App launches also update local usage counts used by ranking.
Classic is terminal-centric. Search groups matching apps, contacts, notifications, groups, aliases, commands and search providers. Contacts and notifications depend on their respective Android access; a permission-related result does not grant access by itself.
Type help to see manual categories. Continue typing to match topic IDs, titles or article text. Tapping a help topic opens that page directly, without running its examples. mode -status shows your current launcher mode; mode search and mode classic save a mode change and refresh the interface. Cyberdeck and CRT effects are separate from these modes.

## Examples

```
mode search
```

Switch to Search mode and refresh UI; this changes saved launcher mode.

```
mode classic
```

Return to terminal-centric Classic mode; effects are separate.

```
mode -status
```

Inspect active launcher mode."
"Read help or follow a guided task"

"Guide is an interactive walkthrough separate from this read-only manual, with basics, customize and modules paths. Start a path, use next/back to move between steps, off to hide it and resume to continue. Restart returns a path to its first step; reset clears saved guide progress, not the whole launcher configuration. Progress can advance when a matching command is observed even if its action fails.

Guide task chips can execute commands. The customize path includes wallpaper -auto, whose confirmation flow can save colors. Use guide -off if guided input or suggestions get in your way. guide -startup-test rehearses the startup menu rather than starting a lesson. Use help when you only want to read.

## Examples

```
guide -start basics
```

Start the basics path.

```
guide -status
```

Inspect guide progress.

```
guide -off
```

Stop the guided session.

```
guide -resume
```

Resume stored path progress."
"Choose app suggestions and launch counts"

"Default app slots use apps -default_app followed by an integer slot and a shown app, most_used, or null marker. The slot is validated against actual Apps settings; invalid indices report an error. The command refreshes default suggestions. apps -reset clears the selected visible app’s launched_times counter; it does not clear that app’s data.

## Examples

```
apps -default_app 1 most_used
```

Change slot 1 to the most-used marker."
"Create a local Lua app or a dock panel"

"Lua apps and Lua dock modules are different script types. lua -new app <name> creates an app template; module -new lua <name> creates a dock-module template. Editing an unknown ID may create a template, so use list or info first when you only want to inspect. Opening an app checks its type, enabled state and approval. Approval grants its declared permissions; read the metadata and script before trusting it. Check runs app code rather than only checking syntax. Export copies a package to the clipboard, which may expose script content; removal deletes the script. Suggestion-only scripts cannot be opened as dock panels.

## Examples

```
lua -apps
```

List scripts of type app.

```
lua -new app habit
```

Create/open a local app template; writes a script.

```
module -new lua counter
```

Create/open a Lua dock-module template; writes a script.

```
lua -info habit
```

Read metadata and trust status before approving."
"Create an app group for a task"

"A group is a local launcher collection, not an Android folder or permission boundary. Create a short single-word name, add installed apps with apps -addtogp <group> <app>, then list its members. Choose actual app labels/profile matches through completion. Quoted names with spaces can be saved, but typing them at the home prompt does not select the group correctly.

Typing a group name alone lists its apps; text after it selects an app in that group. Group tabs appear in the app drawer, and Search can show group results. Removing membership or a group does not uninstall apps. Sorting and colors are independent options: background and text colors are separate, and the older -gpcolor changes the background.

## Examples

```
apps -mkgp work
```

Create group work.

```
apps -lsgp work
```

List work group membership.

```
apps -gp_bg_color work #243040
```

Change work group background.

```
apps -lsgp
```

List all groups."
"Distinguish hiding from uninstalling"

"Hide only changes launcher visibility. Uninstall starts Android’s package deletion activity, including for hidden apps or a literal package fallback. tui -rm removes launcher device-admin status and asks Android to uninstall the launcher itself. These actions are not a cleanup shortcut: removing an app can remove its local data. exit resets the preferred launcher and opens the chooser; it is not a normal shell exit."
"Find a contact without accidentally deleting it"

"contacts is the public name for cntcts. Listing/searching needs Android READ_CONTACTS; a permission request can be declined. contacts -ls prints loaded names/numbers, -l displays details, and Search uses the same authorized data. This output is private.

-add and -edit delegate to Android contact activities. -rm requests WRITE_CONTACTS and deletes the resolved provider contact directly, without a confirmation dialog in that branch. Select real identifiers through completion and do not test removal on a real contact. call resolves a number/contact and needs contact-reading and phone-call access; it places a real call, not merely a dialer preview.

Contacts are Android provider records, not launcher notes or portable-preset backup content. Reading this manual does not enumerate contacts or request access.

## Examples

```
contacts -ls
```

Inspect contact names/numbers; output is private."
"Find apps and hide launcher entries"

"Use apps -ls to browse visible launchable apps in the drawer. Without an active launcher interface it can print a visible-app list; an unavailable drawer does not always trigger that fallback. apps -lsh prints hidden entries and accepts a filter. Choose installed apps through completion: identities can include an activity and Android user profile. apps -frc resolves visible or hidden apps for an explicit launch. App details, Android app settings and store pages are separate actions.

Hiding removes an activity from normal launcher choices, not its installation, running state or Android access. apps -show restores a hidden entry. Hidden apps can still open through intents, settings or other launchers. If an app is missing, check hidden entries, profile availability and whether it exposes a launcher activity. Package events refresh the app manager; apps -ls is not a list of every background package.

App groups and drawer tabs organize entries. Opening the app drawer hides the widgets drawer and vice versa. Back closes the active drawer after higher-priority surfaces; Android Home returns to Launcher Home from the Termux workspace/console. Work-profile launches depend on Android profile access.

## Examples

```
apps -ls
```

Open the app drawer.

```
apps -lsh
```

Inspect hidden apps.

```
help apps
```

See app hide/show syntax; choose actual app arguments from completion.

```
apps -frc <appName>
```

Explicit app launch when a name conflicts; replace the placeholder."
"Use app shortcuts and companion-keyboard mappings"

"Pinned shortcut handles begin with @ and retain package, shortcut ID and user-profile identity. They launch through Android LauncherApps, so the source app must still expose the shortcut. A label is not sufficient to restore a removed or disabled shortcut.
Use shortcut -ls to discover published/pinned shortcuts and shortcut -use with a chosen handle/ID using completion. The Settings keyboard-shortcut panel is separate: it maps letters a-z to at most two app shortcuts each for the Re:TUI keyboard companion. Those mappings are token-authorized and pass icon content URIs to that package; installing the launcher alone does not install the keyboard.
Neither shortcut feature is a shell alias. Use aliases for launcher command shortcuts, pinned handles for Android shortcuts, and keyboard mappings for companion-keyboard app launches.

App shortcuts require Android API 25 or later. shortcut -ls lists shortcuts and accepted pinned aliases; adding an app name narrows the list. shortcut -use accepts an ID, an index with an app name, or an @handle already accepted by the launcher. Check the list before running a shortcut: a shortcut may perform an app-specific action. The old -cp option is not implemented.

## Examples

```
shortcut -ls
```

Inspect available shortcuts and pinned aliases.

```
settings
```

Open keyboard-shortcut configuration from the Hub."
"Browse files using the companion app"

"files, ls, open and share use the Re:T-UI Files companion (com.dvil.retui.fm). Missing companion access reports an error rather than browsing locally. cd resolves a directory through its provider, remembers it and synchronizes the embedded shell. Relative file actions use that path. ls ignores a supplied folder argument: use cd then ls. files -search sends a name and optional type without restricting search to the current path.

share opens the companion share action; review recipients because the file leaves the launcher boundary. termuxopen is an older hidden name for open with the same Files dependency.

## Examples

```
pwd
```

Print the launcher’s current directory.

```
cd /sdcard/Download
```

Change the remembered file directory if the companion can resolve it.

```
ls
```

Request companion listing at the remembered path.

```
files -search invoice pdf
```

Request companion search; supported type interpretation belongs to the companion."
"Run a shell command without confusing app commands"

"Shell explicitly runs an Android embedded-shell command. The command text is passed to the shell, so shell quoting, redirects, and destructive operations are real—not launcher options. It is not a full Termux Linux environment. shell cd changes the launcher’s shell-directory display, but does not update the remembered Files path; use launcher cd when both paths should stay in sync. Hidden ctrlc kills and rebuilds the embedded shell, resets its launcher directory, and clears the root-shell indicator. Do not use rm or su just to test the prompt.

## Examples

```
shell pwd
```

Inspect the shell’s current directory without modifying files."
"Save an alias without confusing shell scopes"

"Home/app aliases and Termux-script aliases are separate scopes in alias.txt. alias -add saves a name and command, defaulting to home scope; place -a after -add for explicit home scope, or -s for a Termux script. Parameter expansion uses configurable marker/separator rules, not necessarily POSIX shell-function parsing. Use alias -ls to inspect mappings and alias -file to edit the file. Removal deletes only the chosen mapping.

Home aliases take precedence over built-in commands, so avoid conflicting names. Storing an alias changes configuration; invoking it executes its content. Save only code you trust. Script aliases require Termux, whose environment differs from the home prompt. Use termux -run or a module termux: source for Termux scripts.

shell explicitly dispatches the launcher's Android shell input with launcher access, not Termux's private environment. Bare unknown input reaches it only when shell_requires_prefix is false. A known launcher command that fails parsing is not silently run as shell.

## Examples

```
alias -add ll apps -ls
```

Create ll as an app-drawer shortcut.

```
alias -ls
```

Inspect stored aliases.

```
alias -rm ll
```

Remove the example mapping.

```
shell pwd
```

Explicitly request launcher shell working directory, not Termux home."
"Search the web with a named provider"

"search.txt defines reusable providers. Built-in names are gg (Google), ps (Play Store with web fallback), yt (YouTube), dd (DuckDuckGo) and u (URL). Use search -ls to see your current names/templates; they can be changed or removed. The default is configured by default_search. Management names are reserved; reset replaces providers with defaults, so preserve custom entries first.

Add a named URL template containing a recognized token: {query} URL-encodes spaces, {query+} uses plus signs, {slug} changes spaces to underscores, {raw} inserts raw text, and {url} supplies https:// when missing. An optional fallback follows => and is used if the primary link cannot be opened, not when a website finds no results.

A search opens a browser or another registered handler and can send your query to that destination. It is not offline cached-web search. Review custom templates, especially raw substitution, before sending private input.

## Examples

```
search -ls
```

Inspect the current provider names and templates.

```
search -add example https://example.com/?q={query}
```

Save a demonstration provider; changes search configuration.

```
search -example offline manuals
```

Open that provider with a query; sends the query to the handler.

```
search -dd android launcher
```

Open a DuckDuckGo query if the default dd provider exists."
"Change borders without restarting the launcher"

"Generated borders use the master enable_dashed_border switch plus per-surface enable/color overrides. Per-surface auto inherits the terminal border color; advanced AUTO colors inherit their role parents and are not explicit transparent colors. Zero dash gap makes a continuous enabled stroke; a positive gap makes dashed segments. Stroke/radius accessors clamp raw values, so extreme saved geometry is not an exact screen dimension. Unified-status border is separate.

Context-aware settings/config border writes refresh the running launcher in place. config -set persists changes; config -get reads stored values. If a change seems ineffective, check the surface override and custom frame before restarting.

Custom image frames take precedence over generated artwork; with a frame, generated fallback fill is transparent. Without a frame, fallback borders depend on border-enabled, Cyberdeck and dashed settings. Color options change fills/text, not custom-frame pixels. Disabling a surface/master dashed border does not delete its frame or disable every Cyberdeck border.

## Examples

```
config -set dashed_border_gap_length 0
```

Persist solid generated borders and live-refresh running launcher.

```
config -set dashed_border_gap_length 4
```

Persist a dashed gap; changes appearance.

```
config -get unified_status_border
```

Read unified status-border option.

```
settings
```

Inspect appearance settings; opening settings alone is not a border change."
"Choose portrait, landscape, or a launcher mode"

"orientation portrait/landscape/auto saves the launcher orientation preference; portrait and landscape are convenience commands. A landscape preference is not a guarantee of split layout in a narrow window. mode classic/search changes launcher mode and refreshes the UI. Duo companion layout is gated by duo_mode; its side/toggle options only operate from the launcher UI, and need a wide landscape window to show the layout. Disable Duo mode before expecting ordinary split behavior.

## Examples

```
orientation auto
```

Let the launcher follow automatic orientation.

```
mode classic
```

Switch to classic launcher layout."
"Edit a frame pack, not a theme preset"

"Settings Frames stages frame selections/assignments in an edit session. Choose an element or apply-to-all, import an asset/package, inspect original PNG preview and choose a frame pack. Saving current, creating new or replacing an existing user pack persists the complete staged setup and applies it. Built-in packs cannot be replaced or deleted. Switching/deleting with unsaved edits has a discard-confirmation flow.
Frame bundles use .retui-frame; UI packages are .retui_ui.zip, distinct from shareable .retui and personal .retui-backup. Frame import validates names/manifest/PNG and size bounds. The editor’s PNG preview is not a full screenshot simulation of the launcher. Custom frames can change how generated-border settings appear.
Local preset save includes current frame state, while current .retui share export does not actually emit frame files. Use supported frame-specific controls rather than promising all frame assets travel with every shared theme.

## Examples

```
settings
```

Open Frames in the Hub; use its staged save/apply controls."
"Edit known configuration files"

"config -file opens a known launcher configuration file in the document editor. The older tuixt command also accepts only known configuration filenames, not arbitrary text-file paths. Use the editor’s displayed Save action; do not use old terminal-editor save or exit instructions in the home prompt. config -apply moves a source file into the configuration folder and can replace XML or font assets. It is not a copy operation or a portable-preset import. Back up first; use the shareable-configuration workflow for portable looks.

## Examples

```
config -file behavior.xml
```

Open known behavior options for editing; saving alters configuration."
"Inspect settings and understand apply versus restart"

"## Inspect before editing

Use settings for the visual Hub, config -ls for file/option discovery, config -info for an option's type/default/description and config -get for its stored value. -set persists, -erase empties a value, -reset restores its default and -append concatenates text without a list separator. There is no -setr operation. Back up before broad edits. config -ls rss.xml currently returns notification values; use RSS commands or its editor for feed settings.

## Refresh and restart

The LauncherSettings snapshot keeps runtime reads consistent, but refresh routes vary. Context-aware border writes (master/per-surface, geometry and terminal border/header colors) rebuild in place. Some command settings refresh toolbars, margins, widgets or orientation directly. Cyberdeck/CRT/vignette command changes reload the activity; notification settings and preferred music app request listener reload. Other construction-time values may need restart after saving or external XML edits.

## Preview versus apply

LauncherActivity.preview preserves terminal UI state during an in-place rebuild; it does not undo saved settings. Transient color previews and staged startup/frame/font editors are different mechanisms. Follow each editor's Save/Apply and Cancel controls rather than assuming all previews are unsaved trials.

## Examples

```
config -info show_module_dock
```

Inspect this option before changing it.

```
config -get show_module_dock
```

Read the current dock setting.

```
config -set show_module_dock false
```

Hide the dock and rebuild it live.

```
config -ls
```

Discover configuration options.

```
config -get enable_dashed_border
```

Read master generated-border switch.

```
config -info enable_dashed_border
```

Read option description.

```
restart
```

Reload launcher activity when needed; not a phone reboot."
"Make text readable and organize status rows"

"Base colors and advanced semantic roles are defined in Theme; advanced auto roles inherit resolved parent colors rather than using one global fixed color. Settings can preview a color before saving. Wallpaper Auto-theme stores a palette snapshot, uses system-color fallback when necessary and disables legacy auto_color_pick after the snapshot. It can replace many colors; save a local preset first if you want to retain the current look.
Status indices are positive decimal values: labels sharing the same integer part share a row. Whole-row edits insert/shift rows; ASCII is kept on a separate row. Multiple labels can share a row. Typography includes base text sizes and global font-size offset; custom font paths are excluded from shared presets.
ASCII reads ascii.txt, supports static/colored HTML and framed animation; enable animation only for a suitable bounded file. Launcher sound has a master switch plus per-event toggles. Cyberdeck and CRT are independent effects, not extra launcher modes.

## Examples

```
config -get font_size_offset
```

Inspect global type-size offset.

```
config -info ram_index
```

Read status row-placement setting.

```
wallpaper -auto
```

Interactive palette-change flow; can write colors after confirmation."
"Use language packs with English fallback"

"Language packs supply text, not scripts. Import validates the pack archive, resource keys and formatting arguments. Missing translations fall back to bundled English. Installed packs and the selected language stay local to Launcher; an older pack version cannot replace a newer installed version. Selecting a pack changes launcher text and layout direction, not command names or flags. External app labels, feed titles, your documents, and native calculator definitions/messages are not automatically translated. Acceptance of a partial pack does not establish translation quality."
"Export a shareable .retui without sharing your whole launcher"

"In Settings choose Create Shareable Configuration, then current active look or a saved local preset. Review selected behavior fields before exporting. The default behavior field set is restricted, but schema 3 explicitly permits user-selected behavior values, including text/commands. Do not call every export anonymous or safe to publish. UI excludes username, deviceName, font_file and legacy auto_color_pick; aliases, notes, notification/reply bindings and callback tokens are not sections of a shareable package.
Save-document export writes and verifies a ZIP with manifest.txt and sanitized XML, naming it .retui with MIME application/vnd.retui+zip. Sharing afterward uses a privately cached content URI with temporary read permission. Third-party apps may drop the MIME; use the manual import picker if tap-to-open fails.
Current export code emits theme, optional UI, suggestions and selected behavior; it does not add frame entries, although supported schema-1 imports can include frames. Custom frame packs are not included in this export route. Use this Settings action to export; preset -export is not supported.

## Examples

```
settings
```

Open Settings, then System & Support > Create Shareable Configuration."
"Import a look without applying it"

"## Save first, apply later

A shared .retui package is a launcher preset; .retui-backup is the personal-backup extension. Package contents and manifest type, not the filename, decide what may be imported. Open/share a correctly typed preset, or use Import RetUI Preset in Settings when another app lost the MIME type. Public import accepts readable content:// input, stages and validates it privately, then asks for confirmation. Import adds a uniquely named saved preset; it does not apply active settings or restore personal data. Confirmation revalidates the private snapshot rather than reopening the external URI. Apply the saved name later with preset -apply. Imported behavior fields may contain commands; inspection does not run them.

## Examples

```
preset -apply <saved-name>
```

Apply later; this changes the active configuration. Replace the placeholder."
"Inspect a shared preset without applying it"

"Open/share a correctly typed .retui to Re:TUI, or use Import RetUI Preset in Settings. The public importer accepts readable content URIs, not arbitrary filesystem paths or private app providers. Manual document selection accepts the custom MIME plus ZIP/binary types when the sender lost metadata.
The file is copied to bounded private staging before inspection. You see name, sections, producer version, supported schema and included behavior XML. This is textual inspection, not a rendered screenshot or proof that commands are harmless. Import revalidates the private captured archive, saves a uniquely named preset, and tells you the saved name. Cancel leaves active settings and saved presets unchanged. Import does not run included commands, apply a theme or restore personal data.
Use preset -ls afterward; apply the displayed saved name only when you intend to change settings. Type is determined by validated manifest, not extension. Personal backups renamed .retui remain rejected; supported old shared packages with a .retui-backup filename can still be shareable by their manifest.

## Examples

```
settings
```

Open explicit preset-import picker from the Hub.

```
preset -ls
```

Find uniquely saved imported name before choosing apply."
"Keep personal backup separate from portable preset sharing"

"## Protect the archive

Settings Export Backup creates a .retui-backup personal archive. Choose encryption with a password if the archive may leave trusted storage; export without password is still available. Password protection uses authenticated AES-GCM with a derived key. Forgotten passwords are not recoverable by the importer. Keep the password outside the archive.
Personal backup includes launcher configuration folder contents and an explicit preferences allowlist, including bindings, callback auth and Space state. It can contain secrets, commands, local data and personal identifiers: do not publish it like a theme. Restore Backup validates the archive and, for a personal manifest, deletes/replaces current launcher-root files and restores included preferences. This is a destructive local restore, unlike preset-only import.
The label full/personal does not mean every app-private asset or device setting. The current Remember note database and Markdown/assets are stored outside the archived configuration folder. Android-widget drawer and companion-keyboard shortcut preferences are also omitted. These are not protected by this backup. Termux files/apps and other Android apps are not a device-wide backup.

## Restore is destructive

## Examples

## Coverage limits

```
settings
```

Use Export Backup/Restore Backup actions; verify file kind before restoring."
"Save a local look, then apply it deliberately"

"preset -save captures theme/suggestion colors, permitted UI fields, local behavior and current frames in a saved preset. Behavior can contain commands, locations or personal text, so local presets are not automatically public-safe. Saving an existing name may overwrite it; use a new name to retain both snapshots.

-ls lists saved presets and built-ins blue, red, green, pink, bw and cyberpunk. -apply directly changes active colors, permitted UI/behavior and frame state, disables auto_color_pick and refreshes the launcher. Save the current setup first; there is no save-before-apply confirmation. Review imported behavior before applying it.

-duplicate accepts only saved presets and prompts for a new name. -rm permanently deletes a saved/imported copy, not active state or a personal backup. Portable import adds a unique saved name without applying it. -market opens a network marketplace, not bundled content. wallpaper -auto asks for confirmation before replacing colors; -static/-live open Android wallpaper pickers.

## Examples

```
preset -save mylook
```

Save your current look before experimenting.

```
preset -ls
```

Inspect available preset names.

```
wallpaper -auto
```

Begin a confirmation workflow for wallpaper-derived colors.

```
preset -apply mylook
```

Apply the saved mylook snapshot; active settings change."
"Separate personal setups with Spaces"

"A Space is a local configuration snapshot, not an Android user account, security sandbox or tmux session. -current/-ls identify the active Space; -save snapshots it. -new duplicates selected active settings into a new Space and activates it. -rename renames the active Space. -switch first snapshots the old Space, then restores selected target files/preferences/frame state and reloads launcher/notification rules.

Coverage includes listed XML roots, alias/legacy notes/search/reply/ASCII/webhook/extractor files, selected UI/app/widget/focus/module/reminder/workspace-launcher preferences and frames—not every private database/namespace. Remember notes are in private NoteStore; legacy notes.xml is not a snapshot of that library.

Creation/save/switch write configuration, and switching replaces selected active state. -rm permanently deletes an inactive Space; the active or only Space cannot be removed. Spaces differ from portable .retui themes and personal .retui-backup archives. Keep a personal backup for important setups, noting its own coverage limits.

## Examples

```
space -current
```

Inspect the active Space.

```
space -save
```

Snapshot the current active Space.

```
space -new work
```

Duplicate active settings and switch to work.

```
space -ls
```

List local Spaces."
"Add a feed and know what updates can trigger"

"rss -add without enough arguments opens a setup form; full syntax takes an integer feed ID, interval in seconds and URL. -ls opens the feed list, -menu opens a feed's options and -l ID prints cached entries. -rm deletes configuration. -show and -wifi_only take true/false; -alias changes the display label. The RSS module summarizes configured feeds with clickable links.

Formats/colors, entry/date tags and include/exclude regex rules are configurable. -entry_tag takes ID then tag; -rm_format takes only ID. -time_format configures publication-date parsing, not display formatting; dates/links depend on RSS/Atom contents. With include_rss_default false, a matching include_if_matches regex currently suppresses the entry rather than including it: do not treat it as an allowlist.

Regular Wi-Fi-only feeds skip updates off Wi-Fi, but -frc explicitly bypasses that restriction. Refresh sends requests to the chosen server. Cached entries are not complete offline articles. add_command regex automation can substitute captured groups from new/background items and execute launcher commands; manual listing skips that loop. Do not trust remote feed text to trigger local actions without reviewing the rules.

## Examples


"Browse calculator help without calculating"

"## Read without calculating

Tap the calculator question-mark tab, or type `help` at `calc>` and submit it, to open this dedicated offline reader. Header-tab entry keeps the calculator draft, selection and transcript. Typed help is consumed as a local command. The reader has its own numbered input; choices and examples never evaluate expressions or enter the calculation transcript. A pending calculation can finish without consuming the reader draft.

At `help>`, choose a displayed number or tap its line. Within an article, 1 returns to its topic list and 2/3 move between articles when shown. Android Back moves up the manual hierarchy; 0 closes the reader and returns to the calculator. Use the header window control to switch between maximized and windowed reading; drag the header to move and the visible edge/corner handles to resize. Text reflows rather than scaling.

## Expressions and operators

```
2 + 3 * 4 → 14
(2 + 3) * 4 → 20
2^3 → 8
```

Use +, −, ×, ÷, parentheses, ^ and %.

## Functions and constants

```
sqrt(9) → 3
sin(90) → 1 in degrees mode
```

FUNC inserts sqrt, sin, cos, tan, log, ln and abs with parentheses. Constants: `pi` and `e`.

## Conversions and ans

```
5 ft to miles
20 celsius to fahrenheit
```

Use `to` for conversion. The word `in` means inches. ABC enters letters and units. `ans` holds the last successful result, including units; errors and cancellation do not replace it.

```
5 ft to miles
ans * 2
ans to ft → 10 ft
```

## Keypad and editing

- 123: numbers and operators
- ABC: letters and units
- FUNC: functions and constants

Tap the prompt to place the cursor or select text. √ and function keys wrap selected text or insert parentheses with the cursor inside. ⌫ deletes the selection or previous character. ↵ evaluates.

- `clear` clears the transcript, keeping ans.
- `help` opens this reader.
- `exit` closes the calculator.
- Cancel stops a calculation without changing your input.

>! Examples are read-only here. Entering them at calc> evaluates them."

"## Library storage

notes opens the integrated Remember library/editor in its own task, not a separate app. Current storage is a private remember-notes.xml index plus Markdown/assets in notes-library; legacy notes.xml is retained as an import recovery copy, not the primary live database. NotesManager adapts the library for status/module display.

notes -add saves remaining text; an initial true/false followed by text is a lock flag. -ls prints previews. -open, -rm, -cp and -lock select a one-based index or first matching text prefix; quote prefixes containing spaces. -lock takes true/false and protects against deletion, not disclosure or encryption. -rm deletes the selected unlocked note; -clear deletes unlocked notes and leaves locked ones. Use the library's share/export for separate copies: confirmation/authentication for protected passages produces unredacted Markdown and attached images in a ZIP. Treat that export as unprotected private content; launcher backup alone does not protect the library.

Print configured webhook names and destination URLs without sending; URLs can contain secrets."
"Wire a module source before refreshing it"

"module -ls shows known modules and dock. -show opens a panel; -hide only removes a dock shortcut; -dock add/remove/toggle changes dock layout, while -rm removes a script registry entry and refuses built-ins. -close closes the active module. Do not equate hidden with deleted.
Script modules use launcher: providers, termux: script paths, or lua: script IDs. module -add registers a named source and adds it to dock. Launcher providers can refresh immediately; Termux sources need the bridge and an existing script. Refresh runs the source, not an offline explanatory preview.
Termux output supports ::title, ::body, preformatted blocks and ::suggest label | mode | payload; modes include command, termux-run and callback. Suggestions can become real executable controls. Declared %RETUI_* variables can make launcher-provided JSON, TSV and timestamps available to a script. Review which personal data the script reads and where it sends it before granting access or refreshing.
RSS, notes, reminder, weather_native, calendar and timer are useful starting panels; current events/weather can be editable script-backed entries. Use module -ls to see what is available on your installation.

```
module -ls
```

List actual modules, sources and dock.

```
module -show notes
```

Open local notes panel.

```
module -dock add notes
```

Add notes dock shortcut; changes layout.

```
module -close
```

Close active module without deleting it."
"Check bridge prerequisites before running scripts"

"Tbridge -status/-doctor report whether Termux is installed and RUN_COMMAND is declared/granted. -setup prints setup instructions. -probe dispatches a diagnostic shell script only after readiness checks. The bridge requires allow-external-apps=true in Termux in addition to launcher permission; shared-storage scripts may need termux-setup-storage. Legacy -dirs/-files/-ls only print a retirement message. File browsing is delegated to Re:T-UI Files, not restored by changing file_backend. Grant only the access needed by scripts you trust.

"Diagnose a missing feature before resetting configuration"

"Identify your surface first: home prompt, Search, widgets-pane input, Lua app, one-shot Termux console or interactive tmux workspace. Their parsers differ. Home widget -add or tbridge -ls does not revive retired features. Check config -get/-info, apps -lsh, module -ls and explicit permission-access actions before changing state. For Termux, tbridge -doctor precedes a real -probe; retuitoken -status checks callbacks without disclosing a token. Configure a weather place rather than an obsolete API key.

refresh reloads apps, aliases, local music, contacts and RSS, not webhook/history managers or every setting. It can request contact access or fetch feeds. restart recreates the launcher activity; live border changes already rebuild in place. Neither is a phone reboot. Debug -settings/-theme prints effective settings/colors, notification/music and font state; -presets prints directory/names. status may lack unavailable system data.

Logs and debug output can expose private settings/input. tui -log requests a terminal log file. tui -reset immediately deletes configuration-root contents and reloads; do not use it, clear-data, uninstall, personal restore or Space deletion as routine troubleshooting. Hidden devutils -check_notifications reports listener readiness; -notify/-notify_reply post test notifications when permitted, not real incoming messages.

"Edit expressions and recognize calculator limits"

"Tap the calculator input to position the cursor or select text. Function and square-root keys wrap selected text, or insert parentheses with the cursor inside. Backspace deletes the selection or previous character. ABC uses staggered QWERTY rows within the same keypad-height budget as 123, and long input scrolls horizontally. Expressions are limited to 1024 characters. The native worker has a four-second watchdog; the client waits up to eight seconds for completion. Cancel targets the active calculation and late results are ignored. A fixed keypad height does not guarantee a visible input row on every short landscape screen.

"Find configuration storage for your build"

"Do not assume /sdcard/Re-T-UI on every build. Play uses app-owned external storage with an internal-files fallback. F-Droid tries the shared Re-T-UI folder and falls back to app-owned storage if needed. Legacy Re:T-UI/T-UI folders are not automatically migrated. tui -folder opens the actual configuration directory or prints its path if no compatible folder app resolves. This differs from the remembered Files-companion directory; respect Android storage access.

Android automatic app backup is disabled. Use explicit Settings Export Backup/Restore Backup for personal coverage, or Create Shareable Configuration for a portable look. Portable import saves a preset without applying it; apply its saved name later. config -apply is not an import substitute. Personal archives/configuration may contain private data, and neither configuration backup nor Spaces includes the private Remember library. Keystore keys are not portable note backups.

"Grant only the access needed by the feature"

"F-Droid requests shared-storage access and includes direct SMS sending. On Android 11 and later, it may open Android all-files access settings before normal launcher initialization. The Play Store build uses app-owned storage instead and does not include the F-Droid direct-SMS command. Direct SMS needs the relevant contacts/number access and SEND_SMS permission; sending a message is a real action, not a preview. Android Notification Access for reading notifications is separate from permission to post the app’s own notifications. Termux and Tasker require their own companion apps and bridge/task permissions. Enabling a launcher feature does not install its companion or grant access. Available commands can differ by build and Android version."
"Duo is an in-window layout"

"duo controls a companion layout within a sufficiently wide landscape launcher window. It requires duo_mode to be enabled and offers on/off/left/right/toggle plus status. It does not select a physical external display for an app launch. A connected display alone does not guarantee a split launcher layout: window width, orientation and the saved layout mode matter.

"Enter names, text, colors, and booleans"

"Arguments vary by command. Text arguments may consume the rest of the input; single-name arguments support quoted names and backslash escapes. Integer arguments do not accept decimals. For boolean arguments, use true or false: other nonempty words, including yes, can be treated as false. App names are resolved through the launcher’s app list. Use the canonical dashed options shown here. Extra arguments are not always rejected: commands with no arguments can ignore trailing text, and text arguments can absorb it. Do not rely on extra words to prevent an action.

"Home, Back and retained sessions"

"Back is contextual: it handles a workspace or Termux console before podcast/profile surfaces, drawers and the output tray. In the Termux console, Back hides the keyboard before closing the console. Android Home is a separate action. In-place launcher refresh preserves terminal state. Podcast filters, search and scroll, and Termux console buffer/drafts are retained only while the launcher process survives. Calculator history, answer and editing position use separate saved preferences. Launcher UI retention does not guarantee that a remote tmux job or session is still running."
"Offline calculator capabilities"

"The advanced calculator is bundled with the app and its definitions; it does not download an engine when you calculate. It is available on Android 7 and later. It does not fetch current online currency rates or provide arbitrary external command execution. Native definitions and engine messages are English; launcher-owned messages can use a selected language pack. The advanced engine runs in a separate private worker process, which can be stopped if a calculation exceeds its deadline."
"Open the manual or a command quick reference"

"At the launcher prompt, enter help for this offline manual, tutorial for Getting started, or help <command> for bundled syntax and configured priority without running that command. help -topic <id> opens a known category/article. Topic suggestions match IDs, titles and body text and open the selected topic directly. Hidden compatibility names are omitted from the ordinary command list; commands without reference text show a fallback, not invented syntax.

Lists show up to seven choices with 8/9 for previous/next pages when available. Tap an entry or enter its number and press ↵. Within an article, 1 returns to its list and 2/3 move between topics when shown. Android Back moves up a level; 0 closes the manual. Examples are text, not executable buttons. The calculator help tab opens the dedicated offline reader. Online tutorial options and companion/network services do not become offline because this manual is bundled.

"Read status, local utilities and focus features accurately"

"Battery, RAM, storage, network, time, unlock count and notes are launcher status labels with configurable visibility/format/row indices. RAM is an ActivityManager readout, not a RAM-cleaning optimizer. Storage can omit unavailable removable volumes. Network labels can have redacted/unavailable Wi-Fi SSID. Unlock count reflects launcher observations and saved cycle state, not an authoritative device security log.
Use time for configured clock output; timer and stopwatch are different commands. flash toggles the available camera torch, requests camera permission if needed and can fail on hardware/access constraints. This is not an emergency-light service with delivery guarantees.
Breach is a local grid puzzle with alternating row/column picks and targets; it does not hack a network. Optional Dystopia uses local virtual credits and escape friction, disabled by default. Those credits are local virtual balances, not money or server accounts, and focus restrictions are not system-wide package blocking. Use config -info with an option name to read its type, default and description.

"Read the manual without running its examples"

"## Read-only help

The bundled manual contains topic text and command reference. Choose a numbered entry or topic link to read it; examples do not execute from the article. Reading instructions is different from typing an example into the launcher prompt, where permission requests, settings changes, sending data or running scripts may occur.
Use help followed by a command name for its current command reference. Some commands also have a tutorial option that opens an external web page, requiring network; use bundled topics when offline. If a feature depends on Termux, Tasker, Re:TUI Files, the keyboard companion or an Android permission, reading its instructions does not install the companion or grant access.
Guide is interactive and its task chips can run commands. Home suggestions and module buttons can also take action on a tap. For private operations, review the destination and requested access before leaving the manual. Avoid copying callback tokens, message content, contact lists or private configuration into public screenshots.
